source: NCERT Class X, Democratic Politics II, Political Science Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. Two Case Studies — Belgium and Sri Lanka
points: **Belgium** — ethnic diversity (Dutch-speaking Flemish ~59%, French-speaking Walloon ~40%, German ~1%; Brussels: French majority). It **accommodated** differences through clever power-sharing arrangements.

**Sri Lanka** — Sinhala majority (74%, mostly Buddhist) vs Tamil minority (Sri Lankan and Indian Tamils, mostly Hindu/Muslim). **Majoritarianism**: Sinhala made the only official language (1956), Buddhism favoured → alienation of Tamils → demand for autonomy → **civil war**.
Lesson: sharing power leads to harmony (Belgium); majority domination leads to conflict (Sri Lanka).

sections.heading: 2. Why Power-Sharing is Desirable
points: **Prudential reason** — power-sharing reduces conflict between social groups, ensures stability and political order.
**Moral reason** — power-sharing is the very **spirit of democracy**; people have a right to be consulted on how they are governed.
A legitimate government is one where citizens, through participation, acquire a stake in the system.

points.text: Modern democracies share power in several ways:
sub: **Horizontal distribution** — among different **organs** of government (legislature, executive, judiciary) — a system of **checks and balances**.
**Vertical distribution** — among **different levels** of government (central, state, local) — federal division.
Among **different social groups** — e.g. 'community government' in Belgium; reserved constituencies.
Among **political parties, pressure groups and movements** — through competition and coalitions.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Belgium = accommodation model; Sri Lanka = majoritarianism → civil war.
Sri Lanka made Sinhala the only official language (1956) — Act of majoritarianism.
Two reasons for power-sharing: prudential (avoids conflict) and moral (spirit of democracy).
Belgium's 'Community Government' is elected by people of one language group.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Prudential** reason = avoids conflict / brings stability; **moral** reason = democracy's spirit.
Belgium has a special **community government** based on language.
